subject: Animation
title: Ease In and Ease Out: Natural Acceleration
description: A fast breakdown of Ease In and Ease Out: Natural Acceleration for builders.

hook.text: Nothing in nature starts or stops instantly. Everything accelerates from stillness and decelerates to a stop.

buildup.text: Ease in means drawings are closer together at the start. Ease out means they cluster near the end.

discovery.text: This spacing creates the illusion of natural acceleration and deceleration in animated movement.

twist.text: Linear motion — equal spacing between frames — looks mechanical and is only used for robots or machines.

climax.text: Ease in and ease out is what separates motion that feels alive from motion that feels programmed.

punchline.text: Life accelerates and decelerates. Only machines move at constant speed.

quiz.question: What creates the illusion of natural motion in animation?
options: Drawing all frames with equal spacing between positions
Clustering drawings closer at the start and end of motion to simulate acceleration and deceleration
Adding motion blur to every frame
